subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The V Engine
description: A micro-lesson that makes The V Engine usable.

hook.text: Splitting cylinders into two angled banks creates a compact, powerful engine—the V layout.

buildup.text: A V8 fits eight cylinders in barely more space than an inline-four by banking them in a V.

discovery.text: The V angle matters—90 degrees gives perfect V8 balance, while 60 degrees suits a V6 best.

twist.text: American muscle cars made the V8 iconic, but it began in French aviation engines from 1904.

climax.text: Ferrari built its legend on V12s—twelve small cylinders giving silk-smooth high-rpm power.

punchline.text: Two banks of cylinders pack more power into less space.

quiz.question: What is the ideal V angle for a V8 engine?
